note: Settings > Change log. One entry for every five site versions (66-70, 71-75, ...), newest first.

items: New League Now > Rosters, right after Standings: tap a team logo for its roster grouped by position, with bye weeks, FantasyPros rest-of-season ranks, this week's projections, season points and rank, award chips, and this year's salary plus future salaries with the escalators.
Tap any player for his box: the latest RotoWire news, his game log with FBP points each week, his NFL schedule, his FBP analytics and a salary breakdown.
Each team gets a Face of the Franchise and a points-by-week chart against the league average, with its toughest loss, luckiest win and record in above-average weeks.
The logo row scrolls away and the section tabs stay pinned at the top.
Swiping between sections works on iPhones.

New League Now > Analytics: points left on the bench, luck vs. expected wins, beating MFL's projections, playoff odds week by week, and a cost analysis of starting lineups (what each team starts in salary, where the money goes by position, and whether the pricier lineup wins).
Analytics tables sort by any column, charts flip order, sections fold up with a Collapse all button, and team logos stay pinned on the left when a table slides sideways.
Game Day > Players adds free agents, taxi squad and IR players, a Rostered players only checkbox, S/B/T tags for starter, bench and taxi, and leaves out players who were inactive.
Swipe left or right on a phone to move between the main sections.
Team records and playoff records stay on one line on Reference > Players.
Scoreboard names stay on one line, shrinking to fit, with chips wrapping beneath.

Player photos on the Scoreboard light up by how a player is doing: a nuclear blaze for monster games, flames for players running hot against their projection, and cold, bust and blank looks for the ones letting their team down.
New Game Day > Players page: the week's top scorers at every position, with photos, FBP team logos, Show more, and free agents marked FA (with a checkbox to hide them).
Projections now go back to week 1, so past weeks show hot, cold and bust players too.
MFL's projected points on the Scoreboard: each player's projection before kickoff, and a projected total under each team's score that updates live during games.
A Projected This Week row on each Matchups game, from the lineups as currently set.
Scoreboard cleanup on phones: seed chips sit on the logo corner, scores of any length fit beside the who's-winning bar, and the record line stays on one line.
Defenses show what they've earned their points with (points allowed, sacks, interceptions, fumble recoveries, TDs) and go by nickname, like Jaguars D.
Names and stat lines wrap cleanly on phones.
The 🥶 only goes to the lowest-scoring team that has actually had a player take the field.
Scoreboard chips for this season's award holders: 1st Team and 2nd Team All-FBP, MVP, RoY, ToY, Player of the Week and more, plus team chips like Top Manager, Luckiest and Unluckiest.
A who's-winning bar under VS on every Scoreboard game, tipping toward the team in the lead.
Notes on the Awards page and the Scoreboard that awards are leaders so far, not final until the regular season ends.
Scores line up in every Scoreboard game, and taxi squad and IR rows are tinted yellow and red.
This change log, in Settings, and Settings sections that fold open and closed.
The mock draft board holds still as picks fill in, then moves up one pick at a time to keep the pick on the clock centered.
New NFL Scoreboard on Game Day: every week of the NFL season with scores, kickoff times, TV networks and byes, refreshing every 30 seconds while games are on.
Game times everywhere show your own time zone (PST, EST and so on).
New Reference > Players tab: every player's record when he's in an FBP starting lineup, back to 2019, plus every FBP team he's started for.
Reference > Records > Season PPG shows every team-season, this one included, with records and headers you can tap to sort.
League data now refreshes every morning after waivers, not just once a week, and a week only counts as played once its NFL games are final.
Rex Callahan's rumor-mill column on a seven-team playoff.
Menu reordered: Game Day, League Now, Awards, Rookie Draft, Reference, Off-Season, By-Laws, Settings.
New Game Day tab, home of the Scoreboard and the new Sunday Ticket Helper: the best three games to put on multiview for each FBP matchup, window by window, with NFL RedZone as the fourth screen.
Scoreboard details: player photos, injury tags, playoff seeds, each team's record and last-three average, 🔥/🥶 for the week's high and low scores, and every team's bench, taxi squad and IR.
Scoreboard week picker to look back at any week's lineups and results, and lineups that fit on phones.
Shared links now preview as the page you shared (Playoff Picture, Draft Order, a column's headline) instead of plain Footballpalooza.
Standings add PB: how far each team is behind the league's top scorer.
Sal's Week 8 recap column.
Mock draft team hauls moved beside the draft board on desktop.
New live Scoreboard: every FBP game with lineups, live points and player stats.
Trade of the Year shows the top five trades as headlines you can open.
A pick used in the same season's draft now counts as the player taken with it, and a player's points stop counting toward a trade once he leaves the team.
Trade of the Year leaves out commissioner pick bookkeeping.
Smaller press box headlines on League Now, newest column first.
The header always shows the site version.
Share button in the header: opens your phone's share sheet for the page you're on.
Record-pace tags on the 1st Team All-FBP, with the best season ever at each position, and they wrap neatly on phones.
All-FBP player photos sit on their FBP team's colors.
Trade of the Year shows what traded picks turned into and how each deal has played out since.
